terms.comment: A modern botanical application, not an ancient American food name. The peanut loan’s stem quantities are not established here.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF: printed pp. 70–73 (food and drink), 124 (refrigerator), 280 (blender), 358 (peanut butter), 383 (spinach). Printed page numbers are one less than PDF page numbers in this copy. The blender entry on printed p. 280 was also checked against its rendered page.
